items.headline: Six TIL therapy companies to watch out for
items.preview: A look at six promising companies developing tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapies.
items.article:
Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy is a type of cell therapy that utilizes a patient’s own immune cells to combat cancer. Currently, Iovance Biotherapeutics' Amtagvi is the only approved TIL therapy for melanoma in the U.S. and Australia. Various biotechs are developing TIL therapies in clinical trials, aiming to treat different solid tumors.
Why this matters: With the potential to harness the body’s immune response against cancer, TIL therapies represent a significant advancement in cancer treatment. Companies like Iovance, Curacell, and Obsidian Therapeutics are at the forefront, each with unique approaches to enhance efficacy and safety in treating various cancers.

items.headline: From confidence to capital: Positioning biotech for the next growth cycle
items.preview: Biotech confidence is rising, with increased deal-making and opportunities for growth.
items.article:
2026 has seen a resurgence of confidence in biotech, highlighted by optimistic discussions at major conferences. The first quarter of this year recorded the highest number of deals since 2023, indicating a robust market. China is emerging as a key player, contributing significantly to the global drug pipeline.
Why this matters: As biotech companies prepare for the next growth cycle, understanding market dynamics and investor readiness is crucial. Companies that leverage partnerships and innovative technologies, particularly in AI, are well-positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities.

items.headline: Fast-track trial approval: a way to jump the EU queue?
items.preview: New accelerated pathways in the EU aim to streamline clinical trial approvals.
items.article:
The EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) was launched to centralize clinical trial applications, but has led to longer approval times. In response, several EU nations are introducing fast-track pathways for trials, significantly reducing approval timelines for innovative therapies.
Why this matters: For early-stage biotechs, navigating these new fast-track options can be critical for timely access to the clinic. Understanding the regulatory landscape and selecting the right pathways can enhance the chances of successful trial initiation.

items.headline: Mouse models and CRO selection critical to de-risking neurology drug development
items.preview: The choice of mouse models is vital for successful CNS drug development.
items.article:
As CNS therapeutics face high failure rates, selecting appropriate mouse models is crucial for understanding disease mechanisms and therapeutic efficacy. GemPharmatech emphasizes the importance of using genetically engineered mouse models that closely mimic human disease pathology to improve translational outcomes.
Why this matters: The success of neurology drug development hinges on the ability to accurately model human diseases. By partnering with CROs that provide advanced modeling capabilities, biotechs can enhance their chances of clinical success.

items.headline: Survey reveals barriers to preregistration in animal research
items.preview: A survey highlights significant barriers to adopting preregistration in animal studies.
items.article:
Despite the potential benefits of preregistration in enhancing transparency and rigor in animal research, a survey of Swiss researchers found low adoption rates and significant perceived barriers. Common obstacles included bureaucratic burden and time costs, with many researchers expressing unfavorable attitudes towards preregistration.
Why this matters: Understanding these barriers is essential for developing strategies to promote preregistration in animal research, which could ultimately improve research quality and public trust in scientific findings.
